structure.title: Hindalco at a Glance: Purpose, Vision, Business, and Strategy
structure.summary: Hindalco Industries, the Aditya Birla Group's metals flagship, is India's largest fully integrated aluminium producer and, with Novelis, the world's largest flat-rolled aluminium and recycler. Its copper business is the second-largest producer of copper rods outside China and operates India's largest single-location custom copper smelter. It ranks among the global top three in specialty alumina. The page states the company's purpose—manufacturing materials that make the world greener, stronger, smarter—and vision—creating superior shareholder value by exceeding customer expectations profitably, unleashing employee potential, and being a responsible corporate citizen. It describes Hindalco's evolution into a solutions-driven company, its integrated operations from mining to recycling, sector coverage, expansion plans, refreshed brand identity, over US$5 billion investment, and initiatives like India's first integrated copper tube and multi-metal recycling facility and largest battery foil plant.

structure.title: Values
structure.summary: The text covers core values—integrity, commitment, passion, seamlessness, and speed—and highlights Hindalco’s Silvassa vertical powder coating line and Novelis’s low-carbon aluminium solutions for automotive, aerospace, packaging, and construction. It details a global footprint of 19 manufacturing plants and 25 mines in India plus 31 overseas plants, ESG excellence with a top 1% S&P Global CSA ranking, and a sustainability-first strategy driven by digitalisation and culture to advance low-carbon transitions, circular economy, and inclusive growth. Financial highlights for FY 2024-25 include revenue of ₹238,496 crore, EBITDA of ₹35,496 crore, market capitalisation of ₹152,869 crore, and operating cash flow of ₹24,410 crore. Business profiles cover Aluminium (capacities and products), Copper (cathodes and rods), and Specialty Alumina.

structure.title: Hindalco Business Overview: Aluminium, Copper, and Specialty Alumina
structure.summary: The page provides an overview of Hindalco's businesses: Aluminium, Copper, and Specialty Alumina. For Aluminium, it highlights its position as India's largest fully integrated player and world's largest flat-rolled producer and recycler, with production capacities for primary aluminium, VAP, and rolling, operations from mining to value-added products, and products including alumina, ingots, billets, wire rods, flat rolled products, foils, extrusions, and commercial plates. Copper is noted for high purity and quality, with capacities for cathodes and rods, operations including smelters, refineries, rod plants, captive power, oxygen plant, precious metal recovery, and jetty, and products such as LME grade cathodes and continuous cast copper rods. Specialty Alumina is recognized globally, with capacity for specialty alumina, operations in manufacturing, and products like coarse hydrate, metallurgical alumina, calcined, reactive, white fused alumina, and precipitate hydrate.

structure.title: Pioneering a Future-forward India
structure.summary: The text highlights Hindalco Industries Limited's pioneering initiatives toward a future-forward India, covering aluminium, copper, specialty alumina, and ESG efforts. Key points include domestic can body stock supply, a water-neutral foil plant in Mouda, green energy-based alumina production, a boehmite plant for battery separators, and indigenous battery foil manufacturing. It mentions a hyperloop test track using aluminium profiles, a patent for an in-house precipitated hydrate plant, India's first green tamping paste, indigenised copper alloys for metro and high-speed rails, and Cu Mg alloy production. Additional points cover awards, bauxite residue use in road construction, a desalination plant, India's first copper scrap and PCB recycling plant, bauxite residue pond rehabilitation, and being the world's first metal manufacturer to utilise bauxite residue. It references corporate overview, strategic value creation, frameworks, standards, statutory reports, and financial statements from the 2024-25 Integrated Annual Report.

structure.title: Hindalco ESG Performance and Responsible Growth Highlights
structure.summary: The page presents Hindalco's ESG performance under 'Responsible Growth,' highlighting India's first large-scale pumped hydro storage enabling 24x7 renewable smelting, with 190 MW installed renewable capacity as of March 31, 2025. Environmental metrics include a 19.50% reduction in specific GHG emissions from FY 2011 baseline, 5 mines certified water positive, 16 plants achieving ZLD, 85% waste recycling, and 39 sites with biodiversity management plans. Social data covers 78,999 global workforce, 1.6% LTIFR reduction, 5 million+ beneficiaries, ₹235.38 crore community expenditure, and 89.2% customer satisfaction (Novelis). Governance highlights include US$10 billion planned investments, ₹907 crore R&D spend, 3.86 million MT highest alumina production, 514 patents, and 30 new products. Includes award frameworks and statutory reports references.

structure.title: Future-Ready Growth - Driven by Sustainability, Culture and Digital
structure.summary: Hindalco's strategic priorities focus on future-ready growth through sustainability, culture, and digitalization. Key points include scaling low-carbon circular solutions in aluminum, copper, and specialty alumina; investing in AI, automation, and digital twins; targeting high-growth sectors like EVs, renewables, and smart infrastructure; and transforming into a solutions provider. Financial discipline, capacity expansions, and ESG commitments are highlighted, with specific projects like smelter expansions and renewable energy targets. India's low per capita consumption presents growth opportunities, driven by urbanization and sustainability goals. Novelis's 3x30 vision emphasizes circularity and decarbonization. The document also outlines four strategic priorities: prudent capital structure, value-enhancing growth, strong ESG commitment, and portfolio enrichment, with detailed initiatives and targets.

structure.title: RISKS AND OPPORTUNITIES
structure.summary: Hindalco's risk management approach addresses volatile markets, regulations, supply chains, climate vulnerabilities, and technological changes. Its Enterprise Risk Management Policy uses a three-tiered strategy: ERM, Crisis Management, and Business Continuity Management, periodically reviewed by the Board. A robust risk governance framework features Board-level oversight via the Risk Management and ESG Committee, which meets quarterly and oversees economic, environmental, and social risks. An Emerging Risk Committee identifies evolving risks, including climate-related ones using TCFD/IFRS S2 scenario analysis. The Three Lines of Defence Model defines roles: business units manage risks, ERM and Compliance develop frameworks, and Internal Audit provides assurance. Senior management implements practices aligned with strategic objectives, fostering accountability and resilience.

structure.title: ERM Governance
structure.summary: The text details Hindalco's Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) governance structure, including board and site-level committees, and its digital, ISO 31000/COSO-aligned risk process. It covers a dual bottom-up/top-down identification approach, a 6x6 risk matrix, quarterly board reviews, and risk scoring via historical data and scenario analysis. It outlines the Risk Appetite Framework across safety, compliance, ESG, strategic, financial, and innovation risks. It describes holistic impact assessment using the 3C+2S framework, internal/external audits, and extensive risk training (8,500+ hours). It also explains accountability through incentives linked to risk mitigation and KRIs, integrated into performance reviews and compensation.

structure.title: Novelis

structure.title: Improving Ambient Air Quality

Material consumption data and trends are presented. It highlights increased use of recycled materials at Hindalco India and Novelis, including recycled content targets and used beverage can recycling. structure.title: 5R+1S framework

structure.title: Strengthening Tailings Management
structure.summary: Hindalco's tailings management aligns with GISTM and internal standards, featuring a governance framework with dedicated teams, engineers, and oversight boards. The report details waste generation and reuse data, a pilot project using bauxite residue in road construction, spill prevention measures with no spills reported, and circularity initiatives including recycling expansion, eco-friendly brands, and partnerships. structure.title: Mineral Waste, Spill Prevention, and Circular Recycling Initiatives
structure.summary: The page covers mineral waste generation, reuse, and disposal data across fiscal years, highlighting bauxite residue utilization in road construction through collaborations and successful pilot projects. It details spill prevention and management strategies, including risk registers, SOPs, CCTV monitoring, fishbone analysis, and performance standards, with no spills reported. Finally, it describes circularity efforts through recycling, including expansion of aluminum and copper recycling capacities, introduction of eco-friendly brands, recovery of high-value metals from e-waste, and alignment with Novelis’ 3x30 Vision for increased recycled content.

structure.title: Strategies to scale circularity
structure.summary: The text covers strategies to scale circularity, including design for recycling, improved sorting technologies, recycling awareness, policy advocacy, closed-loop recycling programs, and end-of-life ecosystems. It also details waste-to-resource initiatives, such as utilizing ETP gypsum in cement co-processing. Additionally, it outlines sustainable mining practices, including the Sustainable Mining Charter, governance structure, land use framework, mine closure planning, local economic development, risk mitigation, and divestment mechanisms. Biodiversity management is addressed through the No Net Loss goal by 2050, Biodiversity Management Plans, targets, impacts, dependencies, and risk management processes.

structure.title: Hindalco Biodiversity Management and No Net Loss Strategy
structure.summary: Hindalco outlines its biodiversity approach, committing to No Net Loss by 2050 under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. It presents Biodiversity Management Plans for 39 of 41 sites, a Biodiversity Policy, and short-, medium-, and long-term targets including habitat restoration percentages, native species replacement, tree planting, community livelihood programmes, and no net deforestation. The page details nature-related impacts and dependencies identified using TNFD's LEAP approach with ENCORE, WRI Aqueduct, STAR-R, and IBAT tools, covering ecosystem disruption, water use, GHG emissions, pollutants, and waste, alongside dependencies on water, land, and regulating services.

structure.title: Biodiversity risk management process
structure.summary: The text outlines Hindalco's biodiversity risk management process integrated into its ERM framework, covering four key steps: biodiversity screening and risk assessment, impact assessment and mitigation planning, stakeholder engagement and compliance, and implementation and monitoring. It details assessments for operations, downstream activities, and surrounding areas, using tools like IBAT to identify KBAs and PAs and categorize sites by priority. The mitigation hierarchy (avoid, minimise, restore, offset) is applied through actions like avoiding sensitive habitats, tree transplantation, using recycled materials, habitat restoration, invasive species management, and No Net Loss commitment by 2050. It also addresses stakeholder consultations, supplier risk assessments, and specific biodiversity-related risks (physical, regulatory, reputational, liability) with corresponding mitigation strategies, including restoration targets, ZLD, and policy compliance.

structure.title: Biodiversity Management Plans (BMPs)
structure.summary: Hindalco reports on its Biodiversity Management Plans (BMPs) for 39 of 41 operating sites, with third-season studies completed for 23 sites, and a new BMP for the Chakla mine. Novelis conducted biodiversity assessments for 19 ASI-certified plants. The company identifies IUCN Red List species and provides data on operational sites, biodiversity assessments, critical biodiversity proximity, and BMP coverage. Conservation efforts include planting 5.33 lakh trees via the Miyawaki technique, a planned 50-hectare community-led mangrove plantation in Bharuch, and a pilot restoration project at Renukoot removing invasive species and planting native saplings with a 98% survival rate. At Aditya Aluminium, over 8 lakh saplings were planted, 33% of land developed into green belts, and a 20-acre Biodiversity Park created, alongside butterfly gardens, habitats, and afforestation on 144 acres of degraded forest land. A Belagavi plant study recommended off-site habitat development, with implementation planned for FY 2025-26.

Education initiatives support marginalized children, PVTG, and girls, with programs like Praveshotsava, tailoring units empowering 2,000+ women, and detailed beneficiary numbers across SDG 4 targets including early childhood education, adult literacy, facilities, and scholarships.

structure.summary: The Board of Directors' report presents Hindalco Industries' 66th Annual Report and 5th Integrated Annual Report for FY 2024-25. It includes a Management Discussion and Analysis covering the company's position as India's largest fully integrated aluminium player and, with Novelis, the world's largest flat-rolled aluminium producer and recycler. The copper business is the second-largest producer of copper rods outside China, and the specialty alumina business ranks among the global top three. The report details the complete value chain in India, including bauxite mining, alumina refining, coal mining, power generation, smelting, and downstream products, as well as Novelis's global recycling and rolling operations. It highlights record consolidated financial performance: revenue of ₹2,38,496 crore, EBITDA of ₹35,496 crore, and PAT of ₹16,002 crore. Key operational highlights include aluminium metal production of 1,323 KT, alumina production of 3,857 KT, copper cathode production of 402 KT, and Novelis shipments of 3,757 KT with adjusted EBITDA of $1.80 billion. The report also notes strategic value creation, awards, and recognition.

It also includes a section on Industry Analysis, though no content is provided under that heading.

structure.title: i. Aluminium – Industry Review & Outlook
structure.summary: The text reviews global and Indian aluminium industry trends for CY2024 and outlook. Globally, production and consumption both rose to ~73 million tonnes, creating a balanced market, though China faced a ~2 million tonne deficit while the rest of the world had a ~1.9 million tonne surplus. Prices averaged $2419/tonne, and regional premiums varied. Inventories rose to 9.8 million tonnes. India's domestic consumption is expected to grow ~12% Y-o-Y in FY2024-25 across sectors, but rising imports (particularly flat rolled products, extrusions, and scrap) are a concern. Outlook projects global GDP growth of 2.8% in CY2024, with India at 6.2% in CY2025, and global aluminium demand and production both at ~73.5 million tonnes in CY2025, maintaining a balanced market. Tables detail demand drivers for China and the world excluding China, and India's sector-wise consumption changes.

structure.title: ii. Copper – Industry Review & Outlook
structure.summary: The text provides a copper industry review and outlook, covering global production and consumption trends, surplus/deficit forecasts, LME price volatility, raw material shortages, TC/RC impacts, production cuts, new smelter capacity, U.S. tariffs and retaliatory measures, and long-term demand outlook. It details China's refined copper production, consumption, deficit, production cuts, and new capacity, as well as outside China's production and surplus. It highlights demand drivers like EVs, renewable energy, power grids, and consumer durables, while noting real estate headwinds. It includes references to figures and a table on global refined copper production and consumption, and mentions pressure on TC/RC until rebalancing occurs.

structure.title: iii. Novelis – Global Flat Rolled Products (‘FRP’) – Industry Review & Outlook
structure.summary: This text covers Novelis's multi-year strategy in flat-rolled aluminium, including investments in capacity and recycling, leading to Adjusted EBITDA per tonne growth from $308 in FY16 to $480 in FY24-25 and net income of $683 million. It details domestic copper demand growth to 850 KT, import reduction, and TC/RC benchmark decline. It provides outlooks for refined copper and FRP demand, noting scrap competition and Novelis's $300 million cost savings target. It discusses tariffs and geopolitical risks, the Bay Minette plant, and long-term demand in automotive, construction, and aerospace. It outlines Novelis's 3x30 Vision for recycled content, carbon footprint, and returns, and references the 10-K and Investor Day.

structure.title: Hindalco SWOT Analysis: Novelis and Copper

Weaknesses are supply chain dependence and reliance on third-party raw materials. Opportunities cover recycling expansion, digitalization, cost reduction, automotive demand, and the Bay Minette facility. nodes.title: Hindalco FY25 Standalone Performance and Business Outlook
nodes.summary: The page covers Hindalco's standalone FY 2024-25 financial performance and business outlook. Standalone revenue rose 12% to ₹93,309 crore on higher volumes. EBITDA grew 53% to ₹12,558 crore, driven by volumes, product mix, operational stability, and strong copper performance. nodes.title: Sustainability

Biodiversity conservation includes IUCN partnership and Sustainable Mining Charter. Responsible production is shown through ASI and Copper Mark certifications. nodes.title: Safety
nodes.summary: Hindalco's safety commitment is implemented via OHS systems across all plants and mines. In FY 2024-25, it scored 94/100 in S&P Global's OHS assessment and recorded LTIFR of 0.26 and LTISR of 93.31, with no employee fatalities but two contractor deaths. Contractor safety management was strengthened through pre-bid processes and a specialized contractor pool. The 'Suraksha ki Baat' initiative promotes safety awareness, and over 473,000 behavior-based safety observations were made. Safety training exceeded targets with over 1.7 lakh man-hours. Safety taskforces with subject matter experts conduct audits. The Apex Integrated Health Committee oversees preventive, promotive, curative, and rehabilitative care. Exposure assessments were conducted at multiple sites, and the PEHEL digital health system was implemented. Digital safety initiatives include E Permit-to-Work, audit software, remote crawler technology, AI cameras, fatigue management, gas monitoring, and a central safety dashboard.

My People Hour held 4,304 sessions, and empowerment-by-design led to 617 and 584 devolved decisions in consecutive years. Digital innovation includes the MetaLearn 3D gamified onboarding platform and WeLearn WhatsApp microlearning. Gender diversity rose to 11.41%, supported by three Employee Resource Groups (W-ERG, Generational ERG, and a third implied). The Technical Career Path program has 75 engineers producing 7 granted and 6 filed patents, celebrated at TCP Day. The HTU Metaverse enhances learning across value chains.

structure.title: 32. Capital management
structure.summary: The Group's capital management objective is to ensure business continuity, provide reasonable returns to stakeholders, and control costs by periodically reviewing capital requirements based on operating and business plans, including capital expenditure and strategic investments. Capital is sourced through internal accruals and a mix of equity and short- and long-term borrowing. The net debt to equity ratio is used to monitor capital. No changes were made to objectives, policies, or processes during the years ended 31/03/2025 and 31/03/2024. structure.title: Valuation process
structure.summary:
Valuation process
Some of the Group’s assets and liabilities are measured at fair value for financial reporting purposes. The Management of the Group has set up a team in the finance department which performs the valuation of financial assets and liabilities.
In estimating the fair value of an asset or a liability, the Group uses market-observable data to the extent it is available. Where Level 1 inputs are not available, the Group engages third party qualified valuers to perform the valuation. The team works closely with qualified external valuers to establish the appropriate valuation techniques and inputs to the model. The team reports findings to the Management of the Group to explain the cause of fluctuations in the fair value of the assets and liabilities.

structure.title: Valuation techniques used for valuation of instruments that are categorised as level 3.

It notes assumptions like discount rates and credit spreads and no significant inter-relationships between unobservable inputs. It then discusses financial risk management, detailing market risk: commodity price risk for Copper and Aluminium businesses, including hedging via derivatives, embedded derivatives in copper concentrate purchases, Novelis's conversion model, and sensitivity analysis of commodity price changes on equity and profit. It also covers foreign currency risk, including exposure to USD, EUR, and other currencies, and hedging strategies.

Section (ii) shows changes in fair value of plan assets, including acquisition adjustment, interest income, employer and participant contributions, return on plan assets, and benefits paid. Section (iii) presents the net balance sheet position, showing DBO, fair value of plan assets, surplus/deficit, irrecoverable surplus due to asset ceiling, and net defined benefit asset/liability. Section (iv) reconciles the net balance sheet position from beginning to end, including service cost, net interest, actuarial gains/losses in OCI, employer contributions, benefits paid directly, and acquisition credit/cost. Section (v) covers changes in irrecoverable surplus, including prior period balance, interest, change, and excess of interest. All figures are in crore for years ended 31/03/2025 and 31/03/2024.

nodes.summary: The text presents financial statement notes on employee benefits for Hindalco Industries, covering expense recognition (service cost, interest cost, interest income, irrecoverable surplus interest) for Funds I and II for years ended 31/03/2025 and 31/03/2024. It details Other Comprehensive Income components (actuarial gains/losses, return on plan assets, irrecoverable surplus changes), defined benefit costs, principal actuarial assumptions (discount rate, expected return on assets, EPFO return, weighted average duration), non-current and current employee benefit obligations, expected maturity analysis of undiscounted provident fund, composition of plan assets by category with percentages, and sensitivity analysis of the defined benefit obligation to changes in the discount rate.

Defined Benefit Costs show service cost and net interest. Principal Actuarial Assumptions list discount rates, expected asset returns, and weighted average duration. Non-Current and Current Employee Benefit Obligations are presented. Expected Maturity Analysis of undiscounted provident fund outlines cash flows by time bands. nodes.title: Impact on provision - Increase / (Decrease)
nodes.summary: The text presents sensitivity analysis of discount rate impacts on defined benefit obligations (DBO) for pension and post-retirement medical plans across funds and years, with tables showing effects of 0.5% increase/decrease. It details defined contribution plans (provident fund, superannuation, family pension) with contribution amounts. It covers other employee benefit plans: compensated absences (leave provision and expected settlement) and share-based payments, including equity-settled options, cash-settled share appreciation rights, and trust-administered schemes. It describes ESOS 2013, including grant limits, vesting conditions, exercise terms, and grant/forfeiture details as of 31/03/2025 and 31/03/2024. The text also includes report headers and page numbers.

nodes.title: Employee Benefit Plans: Sensitivity, Pension, and Provident Fund Notes
nodes.summary: The page presents notes to standalone financial statements covering three employee benefit areas. It first shows sensitivity analysis for discount rate, detailing the effect on defined benefit obligation (DBO) of a 0.5% increase and decrease for pension and post-retirement medical plans for years ended 31/03/2025 and 31/03/2024. Next, it describes defined contribution plans, including provident funds not managed by trust, superannuation fund, and family pension fund, noting contributions to government-administered funds and limited company obligation. The pension section explains a contributory plan with contributions to superannuation funds, NPS, or Birla Sunlife Insurance, converted to LIC annuity at retirement, with amounts debited to profit and loss of ₹19 Crore (prior year ₹18 Crore). Finally, provident fund (other than trust) covers contributions to the Regional Provident Fund Commissioner and Coal Mines Provident Fund, with amounts debited to profit and loss of ₹29 Crore (prior year ₹29 Crore).

nodes.title: B. Other Employee Benefit plans
nodes.summary: The text covers notes to Hindalco Industries' standalone financial statements: employee benefits including compensated absences (current liability of ₹341 Crore), equity-settled share-based payments (ESOS 2013, 2018, 2022 with movement summaries, fair values, and expense recognition), cash-settled stock appreciation rights (SAR 2018), and a summary of employee benefit obligations (defined benefit plans, provident fund, defined contribution funds, other plans, compensated absences). It also covers contract liabilities (advance from customers), other non-current and current liabilities (customer refund liability, statutory dues, deferred income from EPCG, MOOWR, Advance Authorisation), revenue from operations (recognition policy, disaggregation by product and geography, reconciliation), other income (interest, dividend, rent, government grants, gain on sale of assets, FVTPL gains), cost of materials consumed, purchases of stock-in-trade, power and fuel, finance cost (interest, borrowing costs, capitalization), impairment loss on financial assets, other expenses (details of auditors' remuneration, lease expenses, donation), exceptional income/expenses (reversal of provision for legacy ash disposal), other comprehensive income (breakup of items not to be reclassified and to be reclassified), earnings per share (basic and diluted with reconciliation), and government grants (accounting policy, EPCG, MOOWR, Advance Authorisation, other grants, movement of grants, income recognized).

structure.title: 31. Contingent Liabilities and Commitments
key_items: Critical Accounting Judgment and Key Sources of Estimation Uncertainty
structure.summary: This text covers contingent liabilities and commitments, including definitions and disclosure policies for contingent liabilities and assets. It also lists commitments: capital contracts, goods/services purchase commitments, and an investment agreement in a renewable power SPV. It discusses critical accounting judgments for uncertain liabilities. Finally, it covers capital management objectives, debt-to-equity ratio, and compliance with debt covenants.

structure.title: 33. Fair Value Measurment of Financial Instruments
structure.summary: The text covers fair value measurement of financial instruments, including critical accounting judgements and valuation techniques. It presents tables of carrying amounts for financial assets and liabilities by category (amortised cost, FVTOCI, FVTPL) as of March 31, 2024 and 2025. It discloses fair values of financial assets and liabilities measured at amortised cost, and classifies finance income and costs by instrument category. The fair value hierarchy (Levels 1, 2, 3) is detailed for recurring and non-recurring measurements, along with changes in Level 3 items, sensitivity analysis, and valuation processes and techniques for Level 3 instruments.

structure.title: 34. Financial Risk Management
structure.summary: This section covers financial risk management, including exposure to market, liquidity, and credit risks. It details commodity price risk for Hindalco's India operations, focusing on the Copper Business's custom smelting model and derivatives for hedging timing mismatches and currency risk, and the Aluminium Business's vertically integrated pricing risks. Embedded derivatives in copper concentrate purchases are segregated and fair value hedged. Foreign currency risk management discusses USD and EUR exchange rate impacts, derivative instruments, FOB export and CIF import values, net exposure tables, and sensitivity analysis. Interest rate risk, equity price risk, and liquidity risk are addressed with sensitivity analyses, credit facilities, and maturity analyses of financial liabilities. Credit risk management includes policies, expected credit loss provisions, and a provision reconciliation. Offsetting of financial assets and liabilities is also detailed.

nodes.title: Embedded Derivatives
nodes.summary: This section on financial risk management outlines the Company's exposure to market, liquidity, and credit risks. It focuses on market risk, specifically commodity price risk for Hindalco's India Operations. The Copper Business uses a custom smelting model with derivatives to hedge timing mismatches between input and output prices and currency risk, while also managing view-based exposures. The Aluminium Business, vertically integrated, faces independent input and output pricing risks, hedged with derivatives. Embedded derivatives in copper concentrate purchases are segregated and fair value hedged against inventory. A table summarizes the gain/loss impact of commodity price changes on equity and profit for years ended 31/03/2025 and 31/03/2024, covering aluminium, copper, gold, silver, and furnace oil, with sensitivity analysis assuming a 10% price change.

nodes.title: Foreign Currency Risk
nodes.summary: The text discusses foreign currency risk management, including the impact of USD and EUR exchange rate movements against INR on operating results, commodity pricing based on LME and USD/INR rates, and derivative instruments to match outflows and inflows. It notes that INR strengthening adversely affects the Aluminium business and that forex contracts protect profitability and mitigate risks from capital item procurement. It reports FOB export value of ₹16,642 Crore (prior year ₹18,018 Crore) and CIF import value of ₹51,205 Crore (prior year ₹45,715 Crore). It presents net foreign currency exposure tables for 2024-25 and 2023-24 by currency, showing unhedged receivables/payables, hedged amounts, and net unhedged positions. It includes sensitivity analysis of 10% exchange rate changes on profit and equity, and discloses net foreign currency payables of ₹11,746 Crore (2024) and ₹10,229 Crore (2023) to be offset by receivables. It also covers interest rate risk on borrowings and financial assets, with active evaluation and use of interest rate swaps.

nodes.title: Unhedged Foreign Currency (Payable) / Receivable
nodes.summary: These notes to standalone financial statements detail the Company's financial risk management. It covers foreign currency risk exposure for FY2025 and FY2024, including unhedged receivables/payables by currency, hedged positions, and sensitivity analysis showing gain/loss impact on profit and equity from exchange rate changes. Interest rate risk on borrowings and financial assets is discussed with sensitivity analysis. Equity securities price risk from FVTOCI/FVTPL investments is summarized with sensitivity. Liquidity risk management is outlined, including financing arrangements with undrawn borrowing facilities, and a maturity analysis of financial liabilities and derivatives based on contractual undiscounted cash flows. The text includes tables with numerical data for each risk category.

nodes.title: Interest Rate, Equity Price, Liquidity Risk and Financing Arrangements
nodes.summary: The page covers interest rate risk with sensitivity tables showing gain/loss impact on equity and profit from rate changes, and states no outstanding interest rate hedges. It addresses equity securities price risk via sensitivity tables for investment in NSE, managed through portfolio diversification. Liquidity risk is detailed with short, medium, and long-term cash forecasting, operational cash flow management, diversified funding, surplus fund investments, undrawn credit facilities, and internal controls. Financing arrangement section lists undrawn borrowing facilities, including bank overdraft and other facilities, with comparative figures.

nodes.title: Maturity Analysis
nodes.summary: The text provides a maturity analysis of financial liabilities as of 31/03/2025 and 31/03/2024, categorizing non-derivative and derivative liabilities into maturity buckets (less than 1 year, 1-2 years, 2-5 years, over 5 years) with contractual undiscounted cash flows and carrying values. It includes notes on borrowings, interest, lease liabilities, supplier credit, trade payables, other financial liabilities, and net settled derivatives. Additionally, it covers credit risk management, including policies for mitigating risk, expected credit loss provisions with a reconciliation, and concentration of credit risk. It also details offsetting of financial assets and liabilities, presenting gross amounts, amounts set off, and net amounts under enforceable master netting arrangements.

nodes.title: Financial Liabilities Maturities, Credit Risk, and Provision Reconciliation
nodes.summary: The page presents contractual maturities of financial liabilities as of 31/03/2024, detailing principal and interest payments for borrowings, lease liabilities, supplier's credit, trade payables, other financial liabilities, and derivatives (commodity and currency forwards/options) across time buckets (less than 1 year, 1-2 years, 2-5 years, over 5 years), with carrying amounts and totals. It also covers credit risk, defining it, identifying sources (cash, debt investments, derivatives, deposits, receivables), and describing management policies: dealing with creditworthy counterparties, obtaining collateral, investing in high-rated instruments, assessing customer credit quality, monitoring ratings, and using expected credit loss provisions (12-month or lifetime). A provision matrix based on 36-month historical loss experience and forward-looking factors is used for trade receivables. Finally, it provides a reconciliation of the provision for impairment on receivables, showing opening balance, impairment losses recognized/reversed, and closing balance for 31/03/2025 and 31/03/2024, noting no single customer exceeds 10% of trade receivables and mentioning credit risk exposure for FVTPL/FVTOCI financial assets.

structure.title: 35. Offsetting Financial Liabilities and Financial Assets
structure.summary: The text covers two notes to financial statements. Note 35 details offsetting financial liabilities and assets, including the accounting policy for offsetting when legally enforceable rights and intentions to settle net exist. It presents tables as at 31/03/2025 and 31/03/2024 showing gross amounts of derivatives, amounts set off, net amounts presented, and related amounts not offset under master netting arrangements, with collateral. Note 36 discloses relationships with struck-off companies under the Companies Act, listing names of struck-off companies, nature of transactions (sale/purchase of goods and services, deposit refundable), balances outstanding as at 31/03/2025 and 31/03/2024, and relationship status (not a related party).

structure.title: 37. Financials Ratio Analysis:
structure.summary: The text presents a financial ratio analysis with a table of various ratios (current, debt-equity, debt service coverage, return on equity, inventory turnover, trade receivables turnover, trade payables turnover, net capital turnover, net profit, return on capital employed, and return on investment) comparing figures as at 31/03/2025 and 31/03/2024, along with percentage changes. It includes notes on related party status, formulas for each ratio, and clarifications for significant changes, such as increased profit, nil principal repayment, and fair value changes in equity instruments.

nodes.title: Independent Assurance Statement: Methodology, Limitations, Responsibilities, Uncertainty, and BRSR Conclusions
